trial_court: Court of Ms. NEHA GUPTA SINGH, Chief Judicial Magistrate, North, Rohini Courts: Delhi

parties.respondent_defendant: Sh. Mukesh Kumar S/o Mir Singh (accused)

facts_of_case: Complainant and accused are known to each other. Accused borrowed Rs. 15,00,000 from complainant with interest. Accused issued cheques which were dishonored due to 'Stop Payment'. Complainant gave legal demand notice but accused did not make payment.

legal_principles.principle: Once signatures are admitted on a cheque, the presumption raises in favor of the complainant which is not rebutted by the accused.
legal_principles.held: It is argued that once signatures are admitted on cheque, presumption raises in favor of complainant which is not rebutted by the accused.
cited_cases: Rajesh Jain v. Ajay Singh Manu SC 1096/2023
P.Rasiya v. Abdul Nazer &Ors. Manu SC 1521/2022
Kalamani Tex&Ors. v. P. Balasubramanian Manu SC 0066/2021

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the accused to rebut the presumption raised in favor of the complainant.

outcome.final_order: Accused acquitted for offense u/s 138 NI Act

use_for_drafting: drafting a complaint for cheque bounce
defending an accused in a cheque bounce case
advising on the consequences of dishonoured cheques
